html:
The Quito School was a tradition of painting and sculpture made in colonial Quito from the late 1500s to the 1700s. Its painted wooden statues were sent all over Spanish South America.

It began with a school of arts founded by Franciscan friars to train Indigenous and mixed-race craftsmen. They carved and painted saints and Virgins in the European Baroque manner, adding local touches, such as Andean features or fruit. Sculptors such as Bernardo de Legarda and the Indigenous artist Caspicara became famous.

The churches of Quito, such as the Jesuit church of La Compañía covered in gold leaf, are the school's best showcase. Its art spread to Colombia, Peru and Chile. It belongs with Aleijadinho in Brazil to the great age of colonial art in Ecuador and its neighbours.
